name: Character Journey Studio
description: Animal, style and render-quality pickers, a line of notes and your story in; a 15-second narrated film out — the hero designed from the pickers, three scenes in three places, six numbered frames, three shots each driven from a start frame to an end frame in the same place, the hero telling its story in a voice designed for it, a score, and the shots' own sound.
markdownDescription:
## Character Journey Studio

Pick the animal, the art style and the render quality, add a line of notes and your story: the hero is designed inside the workflow and becomes a 15-second film of three scenes in three places — told by the hero in its own designed voice, with a score. It teaches two things: picker nodes placed by name in a prompt, and the second way to drive a video model — every shot gets a **start frame and an end frame** in the same place and lands exactly on the end frame.

1. **Pickers + Notes + Story** — Animal, Style and Render quality pickers, one line of notes (colour, age, what it carries) and the story in your own words; one image node turns them into the character design.
2. **Story beats** — the hero described from the design, the look, four frames in three places, the narration and the music.
3. **Character sheet → Frames 1–6** — the sheet fixes the hero once; the six frames copy it.
4. **Shot scripts → three shots** — each video node receives a scene's start frame and end frame and animates the five seconds between them on Seedance 2.5.
5. **Combine** — the three scenes joined with plain film cuts.
6. **Voice + score → mix** — Voice Design builds a creature voice from one line of description and speaks the narration; Suno writes the score; Merge lays both over the shots' own sound.

data.text: Animal, Style and Render quality are picker nodes: the Character design prompt places each one by name — {Animal}, {Style}, {Render quality} — and every tile you pick becomes a line of prompt. Swap a tile — lion to fox, 3D to watercolour — and the whole film follows. The notes add what pickers can't: colour, age, what it carries.

data.text: Each shot script describes the five seconds between a scene's two frames. Each video node is wired with the scene's first frame on Start Frame and its second on End Frame — Seedance 2.5 animates the movement between them and lands exactly on the end frame. Keep both frames in the same place: give a model two different places and it dissolves between them instead of moving. MiniMax Hailuo 3 and Wan 3 also take start and end frames.

data.text: Combine joins the three scenes with plain film cuts and keeps their ambient sound. The narration is lifted from the beats in the hero's own words, and Voice Design speaks it with a creature voice built from one line of description — change the line to change the voice: a growl, a squeak, an old storyteller. A one-sentence brief goes to Suno, and Trim cuts the score to 15 seconds. Merge lays the voice (loud) and the score (quiet) over the shots' own sound.

data.label: Character design
data.prompt: Character design of the hero of a short animated film. The animal: {Animal || a lion.} Art style: {Style || 3D animation.} Rendering: {Render quality || high-end render.} Details: {Character notes || a small brave animal.} Full body, standing, centred, facing the camera with a gentle expression, on a simple clean pale background with soft studio light; high detail, appealing, expressive face. Exactly one character; no text, no logo.

data.text: The lion who loved strawberries. Every lion in the pride loved meat; this one loved strawberries, and he had only ever tasted one, found by a river. One afternoon he sits apart from the pride with that single strawberry, and decides to find where they grow. One afternoon he sets out — across the savanna, into a forest where the low sun cuts through the trees — following the smell. At sunset he steps out of the trees onto a hill and sees a whole valley of strawberry fields below. He lies down among the strawberries and eats until his muzzle is red, happier than any lion has ever been.
data.label: Your story
Story beats
data.userInput: Story: {Your story || a small hero sets out to find the one thing it loves.} The reference image is the hero's character design. Write the story beats.
data.systemPrompt:
You turn a short story and a character design image of its hero into a 15-second film of three scenes in three places. Each scene is ONE five-second shot built from two still frames in the SAME place: the shot starts on its first frame and lands exactly on its second — Scene 1 runs from Frame 1 to Frame 2, Scene 2 from Frame 3 to Frame 4, Scene 3 from Frame 5 to Frame 6. Between scenes the film cuts. Write in exactly this shape, plain English, nothing else:
Character: <60 to 90 words describing the hero exactly as the design image shows it — species or kind, colours, markings, eyes, any object it carries, how it moves; this description is copied into every frame>
Look: <one paragraph of 40 to 60 words: the rendering style of the design image (illustrated, painterly, 3D animation — name it as you see it), the light, the palette, the lens — one look every frame follows>
Scene 1 — <place, time of day>:
Frame 1 — start: Image: <40 to 60 words: the still — the hero, its pose and expression, the place, the light, the camera>
Frame 2 — end: Image: <40 to 60 words: the same place and camera set-up five seconds later — the hero has done one thing (stood up, walked a few steps, turned, lain down)>
Scene 2 — <place, time of day>:
Frame 3 — start: Image: <…>
Frame 4 — end: Image: <…>
Scene 3 — <place, time of day>:
Frame 5 — start: Image: <…>
Frame 6 — end: Image: <…>
Narration: <three short sentences, one per scene, between 18 and 24 words in all and at least 100 characters — the HERO tells its own story in the first person (I), past tense, warm, simple words a child would follow; it must be spoken comfortably inside 13 seconds>
Music: <one sentence: genre, mood, tempo, instruments of the instrumental score>
Rules: the three scenes are three different places — beginning, journey, arrival; within a scene the two frames share the place, the light and the camera set-up, and differ only by what the hero does in five seconds (a few steps, a turn, standing up, lying down) — never a different spot, never a different hour; the whole story happens in ONE continuous stretch of light — the light may deepen from afternoon to sunset, but never jumps from night to day; the hero is the only character, nothing else has a face; describe any mess from food as juice or crumbs of that food, never as red smears or stains; no text, no logo; the story is the user's — keep its events and its ending.

data.label: Shot 1 script
data.userInput: Story beats: {Story beats || a six-frame story.} Write the prompt for this shot.
data.systemPrompt: You write the prompt for a video model that animates ONE five-second shot from a START frame to an END frame — both are attached: the first image is the start (Frame 1), the second is the end (Frame 2); both are in the same place. You get the story beats: this is Scene 1. Write ONE prompt of 60 to 100 words, plain prose, no headings: first the hero and the place as they appear in the start image (one sentence); then what happens in the five seconds — the one thing the hero does that carries it from the start pose to the end pose, one gentle camera move, the ambient sound of the place; end with the sentence "The shot ends exactly on the end frame." Constraints, as one sentence: the hero keeps its exact look, it is the only character, the place and the light never change, no dissolve, no cuts, no text, no logo. Output only the prompt.
